resources.string: Each target is a service: its apps and its websites share one budget. Days without a rule are unrestricted. Stricter changes apply at once; looser ones need confirmation.
Nothing here yet. Add an app or a website.

{name} was added and blocked. Tap it to set a time limit or hours instead.
{n} apps added and blocked. Tap one to set a time limit or hours instead.

Close browsers the app can’t read
While any website has a rule, a browser whose address bar can’t be read stays closed — otherwise switching browsers would skip every website rule.
browsers the app can’t read are allowed
Type it — pasting is turned off.
A few minutes before each prayer until a little after it, every app except the allowed ones and every website closes, and a hadith about salah is shown. Then they open again.
When on, every app and website closes at prayer times, not only the ones in your list. Calls, messages and the allowed apps stay open.

Times for “your location” are calculated on the phone, and your location never leaves it. For a typed city, times are fetched from api.aladhan.com a month at a time; only the city name and the method are sent.
No times yet. Use your location or type your city, then save.
City not found. Type it with the country, e.g. Cairo, Egypt.
No internet connection. A city’s times need a connection (about once a month); or use your current location.
Location is off on the phone. Turn it on or type your city.
Couldn\'t find your location. Try again or type your city.
Location access wasn\'t allowed. Type your city instead.
These apps stay open during the lock. Browsers stay closed on every website.
Added by you (e.g. Quran and adhkar apps)
Closes the Settings pages that would switch the app off: its accessibility switch, App info (force stop, clear data, uninstall) and Device admin.
While it is off, apps and sites with a time limit or allowed hours stay closed, so moving the clock can’t give you a new day.
Automatic date & time is off on this phone right now.
For when you really want to switch the app off or uninstall it.
Protection is off until {time}. Settings pages of the app are open.
for {n} minutes the app’s Settings pages are open: its accessibility switch, force stop, clear data and uninstall all work
After {n} minutes protection comes back by itself.
On: the app can’t be uninstalled until this is switched off.
Off: the app can be uninstalled from the home screen with a long press.
the app could then be uninstalled from the home screen
Automatic date & time is off. Apps and sites with a time limit or allowed hours stay closed until you switch it back on.
This Settings page is protected. To switch off or uninstall the app, open it: Settings › Protection.

Restart the phone in Safe Mode (hold the power button, then long-press Power off and tap Safe mode). Apps you installed are switched off there, so you can uninstall this one normally; if Android asks, switch off its device admin first. Then restart the phone normally.
Keep the app active when unused
Android pauses apps you don’t open for a while and takes back their permissions. This one works in the background, so it must never be paused.
Android blocks the accessibility switch of apps installed from a file until you allow it once.
This is how the app sees which app or website is on screen, so it can count time and block. Without it nothing is blocked.
So the app can tell you if protection stops working.
Battery savers stop background apps. If this one is stopped, nothing is blocked. It uses very little battery.
So limits and prayer locks start at the exact second, even when the phone is asleep.
Recommended: the app can’t be uninstalled on a whim. You can switch it off any time inside the app.

Choose the apps and websites that take your time. Give each one a rule: always blocked, a daily limit, or allowed hours only. At prayer time everything closes. When something is closed, you see a hadith, a saying of the salaf or a line of poetry about the value of time.
Everything stays on your phone: no account, no tracking, nothing is sent anywhere. The only network call is the optional prayer times for a typed city.
A few steps follow so Android lets the app work. Each one opens the right screen; come back here after each.
On App info, switch off “Manage app if unused” (or “Pause app activity if unused”), then come back.

Android blocks this for apps installed from a file. If switching the app on in Accessibility shows “App was denied access” or “For your security, this setting is currently unavailable”:
1. Tap the button below to open App info.
2. Tap ⋮ (top corner) › Allow restricted settings, and confirm with your PIN.
3. Go to the next step and switch the app on.
Open Installed apps (or Downloaded apps) › Time Is a Sword, switch it on and allow. Greyed out? Go back one step.
Android shows its own screen: tap Activate. To uninstall later: Settings › Protection › Turn off protection.
Switch some on now. You can change each one’s rule later in Apps.
None of the preset apps is installed. Add apps and websites later in Apps.
You can see and fix all of this any time in Settings › Protection status.
Protection is off: nothing is blocked.
Samsung: Settings › Battery › Background usage limits › Never sleeping apps › + › Time Is a Sword. The app has no card in Recents, so “Close all” can’t stop it.
Xiaomi / Redmi / POCO: App info › Autostart on, and Battery saver › No restrictions. In Recents, pull the app’s card down to lock it.
OPPO / realme / OnePlus: App info › Battery › Allow background activity and Allow auto launch.
vivo / iQOO: Settings › Battery › Background power consumption › allow Time Is a Sword, and switch Autostart on.
Huawei / Honor: Settings › Battery › App launch › Time Is a Sword › Manage manually, with all three switches on.
Some phones stop background apps on their own. If protection keeps switching off, look up your phone at dontkillmyapp.com.

Who made it, links, licences, and what to do if something goes wrong.

Blocks or time-limits distracting apps and websites, closes everything at prayer time, and reminds you of the value of time with a hadith, a saying of the salaf or a line of poetry. All your data stays on your phone.
Fonts: IBM Plex Sans Arabic and Amiri (SIL OFL). Prayer times: Adhan (MIT) and api.aladhan.com. Brand logos: Simple Icons (CC0); they belong to their owners.
Save your apps, sites, groups, rules and settings to a file, or load them from one. Loading works like saving: anything looser needs confirmation.
This file isn’t a Time Is a Sword backup.
The backup is the same as your current settings.
